boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: We will distribute 1,200 winter coats to students at our partner schools this winter.
why: A count of goods given out is provision, A2.3 ("counts of resources distributed"); no young person is said to have anything.

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Each participating student will receive a backpack filled with grade-level school supplies.
why: Receiving goods is the program providing them, as in the adjudicated laptop row S196 ("Families will receive a laptop..." -> A2.3).

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: The league will provide cleats, shin guards and a uniform to every player at no cost.
why: The program providing gear is A2.3; no state of the players is stated.

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Every student we serve will have a warm winter coat and properly fitting shoes by December.
why: A stated state of young people having clothing and shoes, the EU-SILC child items (HD100, HD110), so F2.4.

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Fewer students in our partner schools will go without the school supplies they need.
why: Going without a needed good, framed as the young people's state, is F2.4 (school supplies: 42 U.S.C. 675(4)(A), partial).

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Girls in the program will report having enough period products during their last period.
why: The wording of the Global MHH Monitoring Group (2022) Indicator 1, a girl-level outcome, so F2.4.

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Every participating student will have a working laptop and home internet.
why: Device check: devices and connectivity stay in A2.3 even when stated as had (rule 15; adjudicated S240). Tests the device asymmetry CP-12-33 keeps.

statement: Participating families will have their basic needs met.
why: Names F2's area (basic needs) but no specific good, food, housing or income result, so Domain F2 with subcategory none.

statement: Reduce material hardship among the children we serve.
why: Material hardship in general names F2 but none of its codes; F2.4 needs a named good. Domain F2, subcategory none.

statement: Students will have the soap, deodorant and toothpaste they need each week.
why: General hygiene items: no verified source frames them as a child outcome, so they are not in F2.4. Suggest Domain F2, subcategory none, with codebook_gap = 1 (decision G9). If Severin rules F2.4, F2.4 needs a logged deviation.

statement: Children in our program will no longer go without clothes and shoes that fit.
why: Names the goods (clothing, shoes), so F2.4 and not domain-only.

statement: Students will start the school year with every item on their supply list.
why: Names a specific good (school supplies) as the young people's state, so F2.4.

statement: Students who receive uniforms and shoes from our clothing closet will miss fewer days of school.
why: The goods are the means and attendance is the only result (rule 2: do not split off the means), so Y1.13.

statement: Free period products will mean no student misses school because of her period.
why: The result named is school attendance; the products are the means. Y1.13.

statement: With donated equipment, more girls will join the soccer team and stay on it all season.
why: Joining and staying on a team is a young person's participation (Y2.6); the equipment is the means.

statement: Youth who get gear from our equipment drive will sign up for a sport this year.
why: Signing up for a sport is Y2.6; the gear is the means.

statement: Kids who receive a bicycle will be more physically active after school.
why: Physical activity is Y8.1; the bicycle is the means.

statement: Girls will take part fully in class during their period.
why: Class participation is Y1.9 (the MHH Indicator 19 framing, routing only).

statement: Students who receive new clothes will feel more confident in themselves.
why: General self-confidence is Y5.4; the clothes are the means.

statement: Students will feel they fit in at school and are not singled out because of their clothing.
why: Feeling accepted at school is Y3.1; clothing is the reason, not the result.

statement: Families will spend less of their budget on back-to-school clothing and supplies.
why: Household cost relief is a money result, F2.1 (CF-034: money status).

statement: Every player on our teams will have the gear they need to play this season.
why: Having the gear is the only result; "to play" is the purpose, not a stated participation result. F2.4 (medium if the gear is not outdoor leisure equipment; see CP-12-33 question 4).

statement: Students will have the supplies they need to be ready to learn.
why: "Ready to learn" is the purpose; no learning result is stated, and Y1.8 is only for children below kindergarten age. F2.4.

statement: Students will have properly fitting shoes and will attend school more regularly.
why: Two results are named (rule 2: split on two results): having shoes (F2.4) and attendance (Y1.13).

statement: Children will feel dignity wearing clothes that fit them.
why: Changed by the expert panel (2026-10-17): feeling dignity is the stated result and the clothes are the means (rule 2), so Y5.4 self-worth.

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Our coat drive will put a warm coat on 1,200 kids this winter.
why: A count of children reached by the program, worded as having; the count makes it provision (A2.3). Added by the panel skeptic.

boundary: F2.4 or A2.3 (goods had or given)
statement: Every girl in our program will have access to free period products at school.
why: Access to goods the program supplies is A2.3; F2.4 needs girls stated to have enough. Added by the panel skeptic.

statement: Students will come to class every day with their notebook, pencils and calculator.
why: Coming to class prepared is class engagement (Y1.9), not a material-need state. Added by the panel skeptic.

statement: Families will no longer have to choose between paying rent and buying their kids school clothes.
why: The family is the subject and the result is household financial strain (F2.1). Added by the panel skeptic.
